text: Search Search Quick links:AIResponse to CrisisKey Challenges © Pexel / cottonbro Youth Home Our Expertise Communication & Information UNESCO Global Youth Grant Scheme The Global Youth Grant Scheme (GYGS) supports youth-led actions and research globally, and builds capacities of young people Young people have ideas, creativity and determination. The only things they often lack are funds and support. UNESCO’s Global Youth Grant Scheme mobilizes resources to support young people around the world. © Pexel / JessicaLewisCreative The Grant Scheme supports two categories of youth-led initiatives: research and grassroots actions. It covers a wide range of topics related to UNESCO’s areas of expertise. Grant Scheme projects can be implemented from the local to the global levels. This support is provided through grants and capacity-strengthening opportunities during the implementation of the grantees' actions and research. - What Do We Fund? Youth-led solutions with social impact. We support youth-led grassroots actions and innovations that address pervasive systemic issues and crises worldwide, as well as research led by young people resulting in policy-oriented recommendations to support youth development. How Does It Work? UNESCO and its relevant partners launch a call for applications. Funding ceilings are defined to correspond to different scales of action or research. During the implementation of their projects, the grantees benefit from training and mentoring. Grantees also have opportunities to showcase their actions and research and gain visibility throughout the process. © Freepik What’s Happening So Far? YOUTH IMPACT: BECAUSE YOU MATTER - For Environmental Sustainability and Climate Action, the Global Youth Grant Scheme led by UNESCO, in collaboration with Nestlé. “Going Together – For Youth Creativity and Well-Being”, the Global Youth Grant Scheme with UNESCO and K-pop group SEVENTEEN. “Because Youth Matter - Impulso Joven” is the pilot initiative of the Global Youth Grant Scheme, in partnership with Nestlé. Launched in Latin America, it awarded twenty grants of 10,000 USD each to young leaders, entrepreneurs and youth organizations to help them create and implement changemaking solutions for social impact. Join UNESCO and our current partners, Nestlé and SEVENTEEN in investing in youth potential by funding the UNESCO Global Youth Grant Scheme, through a Multi-Donor Special Account.
